notes: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" and "One expression per line, and tabular clauses": run-bvpts line 123 subscriber = spawn(fn -> receive do: (:stop -> :ok) end) is graded violated on both, as 2026-10-31 baseline sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and 2026-10-31-b baseline sonnet-1 graded the same shape. Deciding sentences: "A body of several sequential expressions, or one that holds a construct with a structure of its own, a `case`, `with`, `if`, `receive` or `for`, a comment, or a `fn`, gets `do ... end`, however short it is" and "a nested construct with a structure of its own, a `fn`, `case`, `with`, `if`, `receive` or `for`. Those go on the lines below the head". The older 2026-10-22-c and -d note that left this shape uncounted predates both rules' current text and was reversed in 2026-10-29-check. mix format accepts the line, so formatting does not settle it. `def registry, do: @registry` (run-bvpts, run-jrvpr, run-skxbu line 10) is clean, as 2026-10-31 sonnet-2 line 10.

"Use setup for shared data": run-bvpts lines 111-113 are graded violated, the same judgment call as 2026-10-31-b opus-1 line 173 and 2026-10-31 opus-1 lines 172-173. The test matches server in its head but reads context.exited, data the named setup returned, in the body. With both keys the head would be 102 characters, so mix format would spread it, the same length condition as the earlier opus runs. This differs from reads of the test's identity keys, which are clean. If the ruling goes the other way, run-bvpts still breaks the two rules on line 123.

"Use setup for shared data": run-ddccf line 25 @article %{title: "Elixir 1.20 released"} is graded clean. No earlier grade has this shape. It is a compile-time constant used in test bodies and patterns, not data built in setup, and neither the rule nor the case's check says anything about attributes. Tests still match the setup map in their heads. If the ruling goes the other way, run-ddccf is violated on this rule.

"Assert with patterns": the bare :ok = matches in the private setup helper subscribe_and_exit/1 are not counted (run-bvpts 126-129, run-jrvpr 122-124, run-recgw 121-123). The sentence reads "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front", and 2026-10-31-check held that it does not reach a private helper; 2026-10-22-c and later sweeps counted only matches inside a test block. {:ok, _owner} = Registry.register(...) in setup (run-bvpts 34, run-ddccf 34, run-jrvpr 35, run-recgw 29) is the rule's own example and clean. run-bvpts line 112 refute context.exited in Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") is a membership check, clean as 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-check held.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour": no run has a two-function block or a returns :ok name. Borderline names kept clean as in earlier sweeps: run-ddccf 84 "does nothing for a topic without subscribers", run-skxbu 96 "leaves the server running when the topic has no subscribers". run-jrvpr 105 "removes the process from every topic it subscribed to" checks only sports in its body, with news checked in the next test; that is an accuracy point, not the forbidden shape, as 2026-10-31 held for sonnet-1 line 124. run-qzqxw 98 and 102 name a function inside a condition block and still state the effect.
